accuracy.evidence: Checked NC Y3 Animals including humans wording on right types/amounts of nutrition and that animals cannot make their own food against the plate and maker/eater tasks.

misconceptions.evidence: Checked traps: animals photosynthesise; only-sweets as complete nutrition; ignoring amounts; confusing diet labels with nutrition types.

lab_distinct.evidence: Checked flagnutri: balanced four-group plate + maker/eater contrast; not flagneeds (basic needs), flagdiet (herbivore labels), or flagchain (who-eats-whom).

lab_teaches.evidence: Checked: learner fills four quarters, sorts chicken to protein, picks animal-as-eater, chooses right amounts, spots sunlight myth, orders key ideas.

predictions.evidence: Checked tempting wrongs on single-group plates, wrong food bin, plant-vs-animal, amounts, photosynthesis myth, and idea order.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Checked why() splits photo-myth, sweets-only, water-only, wrong group, and animal-as-maker confusions.

readability.evidence: Checked ages 7–8 kid lines use food / mix / make food; adult names NC Y3 and common slips within family bars.

no_filler.evidence: Checked every sentence teaches types, amounts, eating-vs-making, or a named nutrition mix-up.

mobile.evidence: Checked quarter-plate taps and large food-group lbtn twins; snack sorting bins stay usable near 390 px.

accessibility.evidence: Checked plate/group/maker buttons twin canvas taps; live aria-label on the figure; challenge status uses aria-live.

sources: UK NC 2013 Science Y3 Animals including humans — right types and amount of nutrition; cannot make their own food
NHS Eatwell-style food group idea used only as a child-friendly plate model (fruit/veg, protein, grains, dairy)
